correctness.rationale: C PASS: The actual RESULT.md fixes n>=3 and each finite field F_q, specifies counting individual matrices rather than orbits. As F_q[t]-endomorphisms of F_q[t]/t^(n+1) plus F_q[t]/t^(n-1), commuting nilpotents have precisely 4n-4 unconstrained higher coefficients after two diagonal constant terms vanish. The four first coefficients form a 2x2 H; the Britnell-Wildon filtered-module argument proves type (n,n) iff H is invertible and (H^n)11=0, leaving q^(4n-8) lifts. A nonscalar 2x2 matrix and its nonscalar power have the same 2-dimensional commutant, so powering bijects similarity classes; each nonscalar invertible class has q-1 representatives with top-left entry zero. Split semisimple, irreducible quadratic and nonscalar Jordan classes contribute (q-1)(q-1-g_-)/2, (q-1)(q+1-g_+)/2 and (q-1)1_{char not divide n} respectively. Combining recovers the exact formula and zero criterion, including characteristic 2 and extension fields. Independently enumerated 40 GL2 prime-field cases; finite enumeration is corroboration not universal proof.

Hua supplies canonical pair forms rather than this fixed-element finite-field count. Published general commuting-pair generating functions could implicitly yield the same specialization, but no exact direct implication was located after targeted inspection.

value.rationale: V PASS: A genuine, naturally defined finite-field cardinality and conditional density for a centralizer stratum, over all n and prime powers, refines the known nonexistence test and reveals arithmetic dependence on both q-1 and q+1. This quantitative information is not a routine restatement of the binary existence criterion.

final_claim: For all n>=3 and prime powers q, exactly q^(4n-8)(q-1)^2 [q-(gcd(n,q-1)+gcd(n,q+1))/2+1_{char(q) not dividing n}] nilpotent matrices of type (n,n) commute with fixed J_(n+1) plus J_(n-1).
limitations: Fixing a specific matrix rather than its conjugacy class is essential; q must be a prime power; n>=3 required; no orbit-count claim.
